subject: Request: temporary SLO reprofiling for hosted API (p50/p95) during APAC surge
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@finserv.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finserv.com
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: APAC go-live impact and p95 concern

Hi Soojin,

Quick background: we kicked off our APAC pilot on Friday and saw a persistent tail in p95 for the hosted API. Our telemetry shows intermittent spikes around 600–700ms (target was 350ms p95). This pushed a few critical trade workflows into timeouts and blocked our QA signoff.

Procurement and legal are asking whether we can get a written SLA amendment or a temporary reprieve from penalties while you remediate — specifically for the APAC region during the initial traffic ramp. They want the mitigation plan, timeframe, and any credits you’ll provide if you can’t meet the adjusted target.

Can you send something we can share with procurement? We need it this week to keep our launch schedule.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of Integrations, FinServ Systems
Maria.Lopez@finserv.com

PS — attaching our incident summary (ops@finserv.com compiled it).

Attachment stub: finserv-apac-incident-summary.txt (text)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@finserv.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: APAC go-live impact and p95 concern

Hi Maria — thanks for the heads up and the incident summary. Sorry you ran into that during ramp.

Short answer: we can offer a temporary reprofiling of the p95 commitment for the APAC region while we finish a targeted remediation plan. Below is the proposal we can put into an amendment for procurement:

- Temporary target: p95 <= 450ms (vs. contractual 350ms) for APAC only
- Duration: 14 calendar days from the amendment signature (we recommend a discrete two-week stabilization window)
- Acceptance criteria: real-time dashboards show stable p95 < 450ms for 48h at the end of the window
- Operational commitments from Redwood: 24/7 on-call coverage, prioritized routing to alternative model variants if needed, and weekly status snapshots
- Financial remedy: if p95 exceeds 450ms for the region for > 6 hours cumulative during the two weeks, Redwood will issue a one-time service credit equal to 5% of the monthly invoice for that period

If that sounds acceptable I’ll circulate a short amendment and the DocuSign link for signature. We’ll also include a technical annex with steps we’re taking (KV cache tuning, regional routing, and a short model-variant fallback).

Would you like us to shorten or lengthen the window? Happy to align to procurement needs.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Attachment stub: proposed-slo-summary.txt (text)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@finserv.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: APAC go-live impact and p95 concern

Thanks Soojin — that framework is helpful. Procurement would prefer 3 weeks if remediation cannot be guaranteed in 14 days, but they also want the credit to be commensurate with our launch risk. Can you put the amendment in writing (DocuSign) with both options (14 days / 21 days) and the corresponding credit schedules? Also include the technical annex you mentioned so our SRE team can vet the proposed mitigations.

If you can send that by EOD tomorrow we’ll route it through procurement and legal.

-Maria

-----Original attachment: finserv-apac-incident-summary.txt-----

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: APAC go-live impact — recommendation to approve temporary reprofiling

Team — forwarding FinServ’s ask. Summary and recommended commercial terms below so we can move quickly:

Recap: FinServ saw p95 spikes up to 700ms on Friday (APAC). They want a written amendment or reprieve to avoid penalties during ramp. Procurement is open to a timebound adjustment.

My recommendation (to include in amendment):
- Option A (conservative): 14-day window, p95 <= 450ms, credit 5% monthly if cumulative breach > 6h
- Option B (extended): 21-day window, p95 <= 450ms, credit 8% monthly if cumulative breach > 6h
- Redwood operational controls: prioritized regional routing to spare capacity, enable prefix/KV caching for common prefixes, activate model-variant with lower-latency quantized weights for APAC during window, and dedicated on-call for the customer
- Rollback/termination clause: if we see sustained p95 > 700ms for 3 consecutive hours despite mitigations, revert to safe-mode and re-evaluate commitments

Risks: short window may be insufficient if traffic shape continues to change; larger credit in Option B reduces our revenue but buys runway for a safer launch.

Please review and call out any changes. I’d like to send the amendment and technical annex to Maria by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Soojin

Attachment: p95-impact-analysis.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: APAC go-live impact — recommendation to approve temporary reprofiling

Agree with the approach but suggest we tighten the ask on our side: propose Option A (14 days) as primary and only offer Option B if FinServ can show a traffic projection that justifies longer runway. Also propose increasing the threshold for credit to cumulative breach > 8h to limit exposure. We should offer to expedite dedicated capacity if procurement is willing to sign a short-term fee for reserved capacity.

I’ll draft the commercial language for the amendment.

-Ben
Account Executive — Redwood Dedicated Sales

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: APAC go-live impact — recommendation to approve temporary reprofiling

Quick technical note for the annex:
- Root cause hypothesis: traffic burst pattern + cold prefix cache in APAC region leading to KV cache misses and heavier per-request CPU scheduling on the runtime path.
- Short-term mitigations we can commit to within 24–72 hours: pre-warm prefix cache for the top 500 prefixes FinServ uses, enable continuous batching burst smoothing for APAC, and enable model-variant fallback (quantized, lower latency) if p95 > 500ms for more than 30 minutes
- Monitoring & rollback: create a custom alert (p95_apac > 500ms sustained 15m) that triggers a rollback to safe-mode and notifies FinServ and on-call SREs.
- Expected effort: 3 engineers (runtime + infra + SRE) for ~2 business days to implement pre-warm and toggle the fallback; plan for continuous monitoring during the 14/21-day window.

I’m attaching a short runbook and the latency sampling snapshot from Friday. If procurement wants a guarantee, we can recommend a short reserved pool for peak capacity (trade: short-term charge).

-Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: runbook-apac-prewarm.md (markdown)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@finserv.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: APAC go-live impact and p95 concern — amendment and annex

Hi Maria — attaching the amendment and technical annex for procurement and SRE review. Quick summary of the agreed elements:

- We provided two timeboxed options: 14-day (Option A) and 21-day (Option B). Recommended: Option A unless FinServ’s traffic projection requires more runway.
- Temporary reprofiling: p95 <= 450ms for APAC only
- Credits: Option A = 5% monthly credit if cumulative breach > 8h; Option B = 8% monthly credit if cumulative breach > 8h
- Operational mitigations: prefix pre-warm, continuous batching smoothing, quantized model-variant fallback, 24/7 on-call for the window; custom alerts and an SRE-runbook
- Escalation & rollback: automatic safe-mode if p95 > 700ms sustained for 3 hours; joint review at end of window to either revert to contractual SLOs or extend by mutual agreement

We’ve also included a DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/abc123-sign and attached the amendment (slo-reprofiling-amendment-v1.docx) and our impact analysis (p95-impact-analysis.xlsx). Please confirm which option you prefer and we’ll route the doc to procurement.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Attachments: slo-reprofiling-amendment-v1.docx, p95-impact-analysis.xlsx
